http://www.britainnews.net/news/27936093.text: Home London News International News Business News Search News Network UK arrests two men for breaking into US intelligence hub RT.com 09 Oct 2026, 08:50 GMT+ The security breach comes days after seven suspects in a separate alleged "terror plot" against an American airbase were released on bail British counterterrorism police have arrested two Latvian nationals accused of breaking into a military installation housing major US and NATO intelligence operations, just days after British authorities alleged an Iranian-linked terror plot at another American airbase. The two men, aged 32 and 36, were detained early Thursday inside RAF Molesworth in Cambridgeshire after security personnel discovered an abandoned vehicle and a breach in the base's perimeter fence, according to police. Both suspects reside in the UK and were initially arrested on suspicion of trespassing and criminal damage. They were subsequently arrested under the National Security Act on suspicion of entering a prohibited site for a purpose prejudicial to Britain. Their identities and possible motives have not been disclosed. RAF Molesworth, roughly 70 miles north of London, hosts US military intelligence operations covering Europe and Africa, as well as NATO's Intelligence Fusion Centre. Although officially designated a Royal Air Force station, the facility is operated by the US military and does not function as an active airfield. Counterterrorism investigators have taken over the case, but British authorities have not publicly presented evidence that the breach involved espionage, terrorism or a foreign government. "We're very aware of the recent heightened interest and concern around military sites," Commander Helen Flanagan, head of Counter Terrorism Policing London, said. However, she acknowledged that "at this stage there is nothing to suggest this incident is connected to the events at RAF Fairford." The latest incident follows a much-publicized security scare at RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, where five men were arrested on September 27 after police discovered three suspicious vans near the base, which had been used by American bombers during the US-Israeli war on Iran. The arrests initially sparked allegations of a possible terrorist bombing or drone attack, with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham suggesting there were "strong indications" of Iranian involvement. Tehran denied the accusations. Police subsequently acknowledged that no explosive devices had been discovered, with the investigation finding only quantities of petrol in the vehicles. All five suspects were released on bail within days, prompting further questions about the initial assessment of the threat. Two additional men, including a dual British-Iranian national, were subsequently arrested in connection with the alleged plot. Both have also been released on bail, bringing the total to seven suspects released without charges. The Fairford scare also coincided with Washington's abrupt withdrawal of its B-1 strategic bombers from the UK installation. President Donald Trump linked the decision to security threats, while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio played down a direct connection between the alleged plot and the redeployment. In the latest Molesworth case, investigators also summoned explosives specialists to examine the abandoned vehicle, briefly imposing a security cordon around nearby roads. The restrictions were lifted after nothing suspicious was found. Edited by: Rana Taha https://p.dw.com/p/5PIFq Skip next section Pakistan minister blames Diwali firecrackers in India for poor air quality in Lahore 11/10/2026 November 10, 2026 Pakistan minister blames Diwali firecrackers in India for poor air quality in Lahore Pakistan has blamed this week's poor air quality in its eastern city of Lahore on pollution drifting from neighboring India after much of northern India was covered in a toxic smog as Diwali celebrations saw people setting off firecrackers. Lahore, which is the capital of Pakistan's Punjab province and the country's second-largest city, ranked first in Swiss group IQAir's list of most polluted major cities globally for a second day on Tuesday. The city saw an air quality index (AQI) of over 250 on Tuesday, according to IQAir , which categorized it as "very unhealthy." "Following Diwali, extremely high levels of air pollution in New Delhi and various cities in Indian Punjab, low wind speeds, and winds blowing from the eastern corridor toward Pakistan raise concerns that Lahore's air quality could deteriorate further," Pakistani Punjab's Environment Protection Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb wrote on X. She, however, added that air pollution was expected to "gradually decrease" from early afternoon with improvement in weather conditions and the shifting direction of winds. There was no immediate comment from India on Pakistan's statement. The incident occurred while the workers were servicing a wastewater treatment tank at the plant located in Hosur on Monday evening, Indian media reported. News agency Reuters cited a district official as saying that the workers had inhaled gas while inspecting the nano-filtration tank. Apple, Tata and the state authorities will be investigating the deaths, Reuters reported. Tamil Nadu industries minister Virudhai Magal Keerthana said the incident would be investigated "thoroughly” and “appropriate action would be taken based on the findings.” The minister called for measures to prevent similar incidents from taking place again. Tamil Nadu is among India's prominent industrial hubs and Monday's deaths have raised concerns about the safety protocols followed during the maintenance of industrial wastewater tanks. Edited by: Kieran Burke https://p.dw.com/p/5PHJT Skip next section Ukraine President Zelenskyy and Indian PM Modi speak ahead of Ukraine-Russia talks 11/10/2026 November 10, 2026 Ukraine President Zelenskyy and Indian PM Modi speak ahead of Ukraine-Russia talks India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy have held a telephonic conversation, with the Ukrainian leader saying that a discussion took place on Russia's attacks blocking grain exports in the Black Sea. "India is ready to mediate in establishing corridors for grain exports in the Black Sea, blocked ​by Russian ⁠attacks," Zelenskyy wrote on X following the Monday evening call with Modi. Modi and India's foreign ministry did not make a mention of the proposed food corridors in the official statements on the talks between the two leaders. But Modi said he reiterated New Delhi's "firm commitment to contributing in every possible way towards a peaceful resolution." India's diplomatic outreach in Ukraine war In September, during a visit to Ukraine's capital Kyiv, Indian Foreign minister S Jaishankar offered to help end the Russia-Ukraine war . Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha later said that his country had received four international truce proposals, including from India, which he described as the "most comprehensive." Sybiha said Kyiv was ready to consider an energy and Black Sea ceasefire . India's longstanding position on the Ukraine war has been that of a resolution through dialogue and diplomacy. India has also continued its close economic relationship with decades-long partner Russia since the start of the war in 2022. In October, Jaishankar first signalled that India had "got a little bit more involved beyond advocacy." "We have conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard. We are trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue, but going beyond that to cover some immediate concerns which both of them have on grain exports, on energy exports, on non-attack possibilities," he said at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi. India also holds talks with Russia Meanwhile, Monday's phone call between Zelenskyy and Modi came as negotiators from Ukraine , Russia and the United States return to trilateral talks after months. The fourth round of talks, starting Tuesday in United Arab Emirates' Abu Dhabi, comes after previous talks made no headway, with territorial and security guarantees being the major sticking points. Zelenskyy said he had spoken to Modi about the latest diplomatic developments. "The Prime Minister has said more than once, including directly to the Russian leader, ​that now is the time to end the war, not to continue it," ⁠Zelenskiy ​said, referring to the Indian leader. Shortly after talks between Modi and Zelenskyy, Jaishankar announced that he spoke to the Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov. "Our conversation focused on the Ukraine conflict and ongoing diplomatic initiatives." the Indian foreign minister said.
